$comment: ROADMAP Phase 1A step 5 - collision truth. Engine-neutral canon (Rule 22 / Decision 0002). This is the layer Rule 13 exists to protect: visible action and authoritative result must agree. Definitions only - no engine implementation is claimed (Rule 18). Every number is a tuning hypothesis. Semantics: docs/phase1a/collision_truth.md.

determinism.$comment: Collision is where nondeterminism would be easiest to introduce and hardest to see.

hitboxes.notes: Inside work and clinch contact; never a substitute for a glove landing.

hurtboxes.notes: The knockdown-relevant region; Chin scales resistance here but never confers immunity (Rule 14).
Side-specific by construction - eye damage must be visibly attributable to the side that took it.
Arms are hurtboxes in their own right: intelligent varied pressure damages them and degrades guard structure (Rule 14).

guard_volumes.notes: Covers the head cluster only. A high guard does not protect the body - that is the counterplay against passive high blocking (Rule 4).
Elbows and forearms down. Leaves the head cluster exposed - the mirror trade-off.

guard_interception.$comment: Which guard VOLUMES intercept each move.schema.json guard_interaction value. Interception follows the punch's PATH, not its target region - this is the correction the validator forced on 2026-08-03. An uppercut lands on the jaw (a high region) yet is authored blockable_low, because it travels upward into the guard: a dropped forearm stops it and a high shell does not. That is precisely why the uppercut punishes a high guard, and why the high/low guard choice is a real trade-off rather than a label. Division of labour with guard_alignment: this map decides which volume is PERMITTED to intercept a given path; the volume's coverage extent decides whether it actually reaches. Neither alone is sufficient, and posture identity is read by neither.

guard_alignment.$comment: Closes the pinned 10-guards-vs-2-volumes drift (Decision 0010). The design reference docs/design/boxing_guard_matchups.md describes ten named guards whose coverage changes with sub-state - a cross-arm bar riding low or high, a shell roll timed or late. A fixed guard_interaction -> volume map cannot express that, so postures instead modulate the COVERAGE EXTENT of these same two volumes. The pipeline reads extents and never a posture's name, which keeps collision the sole authority and keeps ten guards from becoming ten special cases.

worked_examples.expresses: A low, aligned forearm bar intercepts chin-line uppercuts: the low volume is fully presented across the centerline.
The same posture, opened by pressure - the uppercut splits upward through the middle. Same volumes, less extent.
The overhand is turned off the raised shoulder line.
The overhand arcs over the shoulder. Nothing changed but when the roll happened - which is exactly the fact the matchup tables kept contradicting.

guard_alignment.notes: Illustrative only (Rule 18): the authored posture set is step 7 content. These four exist to prove the mechanism can express the design reference's conditional rows, and the validator holds them to the same bounds as real states.

resolution_pipeline.question: Did the attack's swept hitbox intersect ANY hurtbox or guard volume of the opponent during its active window?
resolution_pipeline.notes: INVERTED STAGE: the verdict fires when the answer is NO. Recorded explicitly so the pipeline stays total. Empty space is the greatest commitment consequence (Rule 13) and the simulation never nudges distance to avoid it - a wrong-range punch whiffs (no magnetic correction).

resolution_pipeline.question: Was the defender inside an authored evasion active window that vacated the intersected region before contact?
resolution_pipeline.notes: Ranked above guard deliberately: an active slip that also passed near the guard is a dodge, and dodged punishes commitment more than blocked (Rule 13 tier order). Rewarding the active defensive choice over the passive one is the point.

resolution_pipeline.question: Did a guard volume covering that region intercept first along the sweep, and does the move's guard_interaction permit blocking at that height?
resolution_pipeline.notes: 'First along the sweep' is what makes a guard a physical object rather than a status flag. Blocked force still absorbs into arms and guard structure - blocking reduces clean damage without erasing consequence (Rule 14).

resolution_pipeline.question: Contact reached a hurtbox: how well aligned was it?
resolution_pipeline.notes: Terminal dispatch into exactly one of the four landed classes. Grazed and brushed remain meaningful damage, not free hits (Rule 14).

quality_bands.notes: Glancing contact; reduced but potentially meaningful.
Full authored force. A visible miss can never arrive here - the sweep stage already terminated it (Rule 13).

closing_velocity.$comment: Rule 14: movement into a punch may increase consequence; movement away may reduce it. Bounded so it modulates rather than dominates contact quality.

prohibitions: Classify a visible miss as a clean hit, or any landed class (Rule 13).
Apply magnetic range correction, hitbox inflation, or target snapping to make an attempt connect.
Resolve contact by discrete per-tick sampling; a fast punch must not tunnel through a hurtbox between ticks.
Replace per-region hurtboxes with a single generic health volume (Rule 14).
Grant an unblockable-by-design attack; move.schema.json marks that value prohibited (Rule 11).
Award a guard break to predictable single-action spam rather than to intelligent varied pressure (Rule 14).
Apply a flat random knockout roll at the moment of contact (Rule 14).
Branch collision resolution on a guard posture's identity rather than on the coverage extents that posture produces.
Let iteration order, container layout, frame rate or wall-clock time affect any classification.

invariants.statement: The pipeline is a total ordered function: every attack resolves to exactly one of the seven contact classes, and every class is reachable.
Non-intersection terminates at whiffed before any landed class can be considered; a visible miss can never be classified as a clean hit.
Every hurtbox maps to a declared condition region, and every physically strikeable region has a hurtbox. No generic health volume exists.
A block requires a guard volume covering the struck region to intercept first along the swept path; guard is an object in space, not a status flag.
Every guard volume absorbs into arms and guard integrity; blocking reduces clean damage without erasing consequence.

Guard postures influence collision only by modulating the coverage extents of the declared guard volumes. The pipeline never reads a posture identity; no alignment state may zero a volume, and none may extend one past its own structure.
The classes this pipeline emits are exactly the seven of data/contact_classes.json, whose commitment consequence strictly increases blocked -> dodged -> whiffed.
Quality bands tile alignment [0,1] with no gap or overlap, and delivered force increases strictly brushed -> grazed -> solid -> clean.
Every region the move table targets has a hurtbox, and every guard_interaction value the move table uses is covered by guard_coverage.
Contact is tested along continuous swept paths, all attacks on a tick resolve against one pre-tick snapshot, and evaluation order is fixed - so the authoritative log is reproducible.
Movement into a punch increases consequence and movement away reduces it, within bounded multipliers that modulate rather than dominate.
